name: Hindustan Unilever Ltd
title: Hindustan Unilever Ltd - 500696 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: HUL posted 15% USG and 7% UVG on 8% price, with EBITDA margin 22.6% (down 40bp QoQ) and gross margin down ~400bp YoY; pricing is pass-through, not expansion.

triggers.label: Rural growth sequentially rising
triggers.quote: we have actually seen a sequential increase in our rural growth and our rural demand is on the rise

triggers.quote: We expect medium -term EBITDA Margin to be within the current guided range of 22% to 24%.

triggers.quote: The contraction close to 400 basis points that we are seeing this quarter is quite high

summary.headline: HUL Q2 FY27 underlying sales growth of 15% with 7% volume growth; PAT before exceptionals up 9% to Rs 2,795 crore.
summary.overview: HUL reported Q2 FY27 turnover of Rs 18,071 crore, with 15% USG (its highest in 14 quarters) and 7% UVG, despite roughly 8% price growth. EBITDA margin was 22.6%, within the guided 22-24% range, down about 140 bps YoY and 40 bps QoQ as gross margin fell about 400 bps on input cost inflation. EBITDA rose 8% to Rs 4,089 crore and PAT before exceptionals rose 9%; reported PAT was flat because the base quarter had Rs 273 crore of one-off tax gains. Management said it passed through absolute cost increases, protected volumes, and offset gross margin pressure with A&P productivity and overhead leverage.

segments.name: Home Care
segments.commentary: USG 22% on double-digit UVG; Fabric Wash grew double digit across bars, powders and liquids. Management cut Home Care A&P by about Rs 250 crore in the quarter; segment absolute EBIT margin about 16% on revenue near Rs 7,000 crore.

segments.name: Beauty & Wellbeing
segments.commentary: USG 16% on double-digit UVG, with Hair Care accelerating. Health & Wellbeing was subdued; OZiva's 2-year CAGR is beyond strong double digits but growth is non-linear.

segments.name: Personal Care
segments.commentary: USG 9%. Skin Cleansing grew double digit with volume-led growth in Pears and Dove bars; Oral Care grew low single digit with premium innovations up double digit.

segments.name: Foods
segments.commentary: USG 9% on low-single-digit UVG. Coffee grew high single digit; mass tea was soft while Red Label Instant Tea scaled; Lifestyle Nutrition grew double digit.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term EBITDA margin expected within the current guided range of 22% to 24%; management said cyclical dips can take margin to the lower end.
Management expects commodity inflation to remain elevated, but does not expect inflation of the scale seen in June and September quarters to recur.
Calibrated price increases to continue in measured steps if inflation rises.
Structurally, portfolio mix is expected to lift gross margin over a 3 to 5 year horizon; no numeric target given.
About 10% A&P productivity savings expected from non-working media, AI tools and buying efficiency.
Confident of growing ahead of the market under the Winning In New India strategy.
capex_capacity: Added 30,000 general trade outlets in the quarter.
Modern trade category-development asset deployment nearly doubled over the last two quarters.
Horlicks Protein Powder launched in the quarter; early traction encouraging.
Kissan condiments relaunched with new packaging.
demand_pricing: Price growth about 8% in the quarter; volume growth held at 7% despite it.
Management said rural growth rose sequentially and rural is growing alongside urban; growth described as broad-based across categories, channels and geographies.
Mass tea was hit by high tea inflation; price increases in tea largely taken per management.
Quick commerce players are supplied mostly direct; premium channel expansion seen as beneficial.
Market shares improved at company level and in Home Care per management.
SOV:SOM ratio on traditional media moved from 1 to 1.1.

qa_highlights.question: Is volume growth at risk given inflation and price hikes, especially in rural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited sequential improvement in volume momentum and rising rural demand, with growth broad-based across urban and rural and categories.

qa_highlights.question: Have gross margins bottomed, and will more pricing be needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pricing covers absolute cost increases; EBITDA margin fell only 40 bps QoQ; structural portfolio mix should support margins in the medium term.

qa_highlights.question: Does the ~8% price increase fully cover cost inflation, and can gross margin return toward 50-51%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said costs are covered; tea pricing largely taken. It declined to give a numeric gross margin target and pointed to a 3 to 5 year structural improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Home Care profit growth lagged strong volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a price-versus-cost lag from petrochemical-linked inputs and said Home Care remains structurally premium; it declined to guide Home Care margin back toward 19-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Lifebuoy underperforming, and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said soaps cleansing grew double digit sequentially and Lifebuoy faces uptrading within its own portfolio; it cited Lifebuoy Ice Bath launch and further work to stay competitive.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25% pre-COVID peak margin a reasonable 3 to 5 year aspiration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 22-24% range was widened by 50 bps each side for cyclicality, with a structural shift toward higher-margin categories over 3 to 5 years, but gave no numeric aspiration.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from elevated commodity inflation, especially petrochemical-linked Home Care inputs and tea.
Home Care EBIT growth has moderated while volumes are strong; margin recovery depends on price catching up with cost.
Possible volume rebalancing as price increases continue; monsoon and food inflation impact on rural demand.
Health & Wellbeing subdued; OZiva growth non-linear.
Lifebuoy and mass soaps competitiveness; mass tea softness.
Reduced A&P in Home Care and rising spend elsewhere; SOV:SOM trend to monitor.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume and top-line momentum, with management repeatedly framing margin pressure as a timing lag from input costs. Evasive on numeric gross margin, Home Care margin and Lifebuoy specifics, and declined to give targets beyond the 22-24% EBITDA margin range.
key_quotes: So, in spite of 8% price growth that we had, we still delivered a 7% UVG, and that's helped us deliver not just the top line, but absolute profit growth as well.
You can recover margin in a hurry. You don't recover market share and growth in a hurry.
Structurally, our Home Care business is extremely well placed.

financial_highlights.change: Base period included Rs 273 crore one-off tax gains

adds.what: 30,000 general trade outlets added in the quarter (distribution reach, not productive capacity)

growth.why: Management guides only to a medium-term EBITDA margin of 22-24% (held) and says it is confident of growing ahead of the market; no numeric revenue guidance, and growth is backed by Q2 volume (7% UVG), price (~8%), share gains and 30,000 new outlets rather than productive capacity or order book.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin 22.6% (-140 bps YoY, -40 bps QoQ) with gross margin down about 400 bps; mgmt holds 22-24% range and says structural mix lifts gross margin over 3-5 years, but gave no numeric target, and Home Care margin recovery depends on price catching cost.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No productive capacity additions discussed; the 30,000 new general trade outlets are distribution reach, not plants or lines, and no utilisation figure was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 UVG 7% (H1 UVG 6%) with sequential momentum improving, rural growing alongside urban, and about 30,000 outlets added, though price growth of ~8% could weigh on volume.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed in the call and no utilisation level was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Only guidance is the medium-term EBITDA margin of 22-24%, held unchanged, and no numeric revenue guidance was given, so there is no stated trigger for an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management expects commodity inflation to stay elevated, Home Care profit growth has lagged volume, and cyclical dips can take margin to the lower end of 22-24%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Horlicks Protein Powder launched this quarter with encouraging early traction, Kissan condiments relaunched, and Lifebuoy Ice Bath is cited as a launch.

rows.label: Calibrated further price increases if inflation rises
rows.why: About 8% price growth in Q2 covered absolute cost increases, and management said further price moves will come in measured steps if inflation rises, with tea pricing largely taken.

rows.label: A&P productivity savings of about 10%
rows.why: Management expects about 10% A&P productivity savings from non-working media, AI tools and buying efficiency, which helps offset gross margin pressure.

rows.label: Modern trade and premium channel expansion
rows.why: Modern trade category-development asset deployment nearly doubled over the last two quarters, and premium channel expansion is seen as beneficial.

tone.note: Management was confident on volume (7% UVG), share gains and the 22-24% margin range, but evasive on numeric gross margin, Home Care margin (no guide back to 19-20%) and Lifebuoy specifics; analysts pushed on whether pricing covers cost and how far gross margin can recover.
